assumptions: The recognition site is the enzyme's canonical one, on either strand.
limits: Finds the sites to domesticate; it does not recode them.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which of each part's Type-IIS sites are the flanking sites the assembly needs and which are internal sites that will mis-cut it?

description: Check parts BEFORE a Type-IIS assembly: how many recognition sites each carries, which of them are the two deliberate flanking sites and which are internal sites that will mis-cut the part. This is what answers “why will this assembly not work” — an internal site has to be domesticated (silently recoded) before the reaction can be trusted.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

enzyme.description: the Type-IIS enzyme the assembly will use.

parts.description: the parts to check — wire upstream `record` outputs here, or list library document names/ids.

name: check_golden_gate_parts

internalSiteCount.description: internal sites across all parts — the number that must reach zero

needsDomestication.description: the parts carrying internal sites, each with every offending site's position and strand

parts.description: one row per part: site count, internal-site count, whether it is assembly-ready, and the problem when it is not

ready.description: true when every part carries exactly its two flanking sites
